The difluprednate group showed significantly greater reductions in subfoveal choroidal thickness and improvements in 3-mm microperimetry thresholds compared with the observation group ( P = 0.012 and P = 0.022, respectively). It also demonstrated the largest decrease in central macular thickness, although this was not statistically significant ( P = 0.19). Ocular hypertension developed in 30% of difluprednate-treated eyes and was controlled with topical antiglaucoma medication.

Conclusion

Topical difluprednate produced superior anatomical and functional improvements in subretinal fluid resolution, subfoveal choroidal thickness reduction, and retinal sensitivity within 3-mm when compared with oral eplerenone and observation. Thus, with a manageable safety profile, it may serve as an effective therapeutic option for cCSCR.

records.title: REAL-WORLD RETINAL VASCULITIS EVENTS REPORTED WITH FDA-APPROVED INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VEGF AND COMPLEMENT INHIBITOR AGENTS: An Analysis of FAERS Data.

content.title: REAL-WORLD RETINAL VASCULITIS EVENTS REPORTED WITH FDA-APPROVED INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VEGF AND COMPLEMENT INHIBITOR AGENTS: An Analysis of FAERS Data.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To analyze real-world Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data for retinal vasculitis associated with approved intravitreal (IVT) anti-VEGF agents and complement inhibitors in the United States.

Methods

This retrospective study used the publicly available FAERS database to identify serious adverse events related to IVT anti-VEGF and complement inhibitor agents reported between January 2020 and December 2025. Reports for brolucizumab, faricimab, aflibercept, ranibizumab, pegcetacoplan, and avacincaptad pegol were analyzed, with data for aflibercept and ranibizumab also reviewed from 2010 to 2019. Events were filtered to include only those linked exclusively to a single agent. Retinal vasculitis adverse events (RVAEs) were identified using broad search terms related to vasculitis, while vascular occlusions without inflammation were excluded.

Results

FAERS data from January 2010 to December 2025 showed reported RVAEs across all included IVT therapies, with increased reporting after 2019. From January 2020 to December 2025, 554 RVAEs were identified among anti-VEGF reference products and complement inhibitors. Anti-VEGF reference products accounted for 485 reports (87.5%), and complement inhibitors accounted for 69 (12.5%). Brolucizumab accounted for the largest proportion (56.1%; 311/554), followed by faricimab (16.4%; 91/554), pegcetacoplan (11.9%; 66/554), aflibercept 2 mg (8.7%; 48/554), aflibercept 8 mg (4.2%; 23/554), ranibizumab (2.2%; 12/554), and avacincaptad pegol (0.5%; 3/554). Separate biosimilar analysis identified one aflibercept biosimilar RVAE and no ranibizumab biosimilar RVAEs during this updated study period overall.

Conclusions

FAERS reporting identified RVAEs across included IVT therapies, but cannot establish incidence, causality, or comparative risk, underscoring the need for vigilant reporting and ongoing post-marketing safety surveillance.

records.title: COMPARISON OF TRACTION FORCES IN EX VIVO VITRECTOMY USING 25+®G 20K CPM DUAL-BLADE AND 25+®G 10K CPM SINGLE-BLADE VITRECTOMY PROBES.

content.title: COMPARISON OF TRACTION FORCES IN EX VIVO VITRECTOMY USING 25+®G 20K CPM DUAL-BLADE AND 25+®G 10K CPM SINGLE-BLADE VITRECTOMY PROBES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare vitreous traction forces generated by a 25+® gauge (G) 20,000 cuts per minute (CPM) dual-blade vitrectomy probe (HYPERVIT®) and a 25+®G 10,000 CPM single-blade vitrectomy probe (Advanced ULTRAVIT®) under flow-matched conditions.

Methods

Bovine vitreous was used in a simulated ex vivo vitrectomy model. Each probe (n=10 per type) engaged vitreous within a balanced salt solution (BSS®) chamber, while a force sensor recorded traction forces. Vacuum levels were set at 260 mmHg (dual-blade) and 340 mmHg (single-blade) to achieve flow-matching, and traction forces were measured across percentiles.

Results

Under flow-matched conditions, the dual-blade probe exhibited lower traction forces. Excluding forces <0.5 millinewton (mN), the 90th, 95th, and 99th percentile forces were 12.8%, 14.4%, and 14.4% lower, respectively (p<0.05). Overall mean, mean peak, and mean maximum forces were lowered by 8.01%, 15.78%, and 12.22%, respectively (p<0.05). The single-blade probe recorded traction forces of 1.60 ± 0.07 mN, 2.93 ± 0.14 mN, and 6.97 ± 0.38 mN, respectively. Whereas the dual-blade probe showed 1.47 ± 0.04 mN, 2.46 ± 0.12 mN, and 6.12 ± 0.26 mN (p<0.05).

Conclusion

The 25+G 20K CPM dual-blade probe generated lower traction forces than the 25+G 10K CPM single-blade probe under flow-matched conditions.

records.title: Regional and Temporal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity after Panretinal Photocoagulation in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Widefield SS-OCTA Study.

content.title: Regional and Temporal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity after Panretinal Photocoagulation in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Widefield SS-OCTA Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the changes in choroidal vasculature after panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) using widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA).

Methods

Thirty eyes of 30 PDR patients were enrolled and underwent SS-OCTA examination before PRP, and at 1 month and 3 months after PRP. Twenty-two age-matched healthy volunteers served as controls. Choroidal thickness (ChT), choroidal vascular volume (CVV), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), choroidal stromal volume (CSV), choriocapillaris flow deficit percentage (CC FD%), and central macular thickness (CMT) were automatically measured within concentric rings of 2.5, 5, 12, and 19 mm centered on the fovea.

Results

Post-PRP choroidal changes showed distinct regional specificity and time dependence. In the periphery (12-19 mm): CVV decreased (-5.45% at 1 month, P=0.045; -8.23% at 3 months, P<0.001); CC FD% increased (+48.9% at 1 month, +80.7% at 3 months, both P<0.001); CVI decreased only at 3 months (-3.57%, P=0.011); CSV remained unchanged. In the central region (0-2.5 mm): except for a mild decrease in CVV at 3 months (-4.01%, P=0.009), all other parameters showed no significant changes. CMT progressively increased (+7.49 7.50% at 1 month, +12.32% at 3 months, both P<0.01). Exploratory analysis showed that centralΔCVV was independently positively correlated withΔCMT (β=0.219P=0.002) Exploratory regression analysis showed that baseline CMT and central ΔCVV were independently associated with ΔCMT (β=0.352, P=0.041; B=528.414, P=0.002, respectively).

Conclusion

PRP induces "vessel-first atrophy" in the periphery with relative central preservation, supporting hemodynamic redistribution. Widefield SS-OCTA effectively evaluates post-PRP choroidal changes. The association between central choroidal vascular volume change and macular edema requires further investigation.

records.title: EVALUATING CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE COVERAGE COMBINED WITH EARLY VITRECTOMY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PERFORATING GLOBE INJURIES.

content.title: EVALUATING CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE COVERAGE COMBINED WITH EARLY VITRECTOMY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PERFORATING GLOBE INJURIES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of a surgical approach combining amniotic membrane coverage with early vitrectomy under low perfusion pressure in patients with perforating globe injuries.

Methods

The study involved 19 patients who presented with Zone 3 exit wounds of globe injuries. The surgical procedures included the administration of recombinant tissue plasminogen activator for hemorrhage clearance, pars plana vitrectomy, internal limiting membrane peeling or retinectomy depending on the presence of proliferative vitreoretinopathy, application of amniotic membrane over the exit wound, and intraocular tamponade injection. The postoperative follow-up period extended over 6 months.

Results

Anatomical success, defined as retinal reattachment, was achieved in 89.5% of cases, with a 100% rate of globe survival. The incidence of postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy was 10.5%. Best-corrected visual acuity improved in 89.47% of patients.

Conclusion

The combination of amniotic membrane coverage with early vitrectomy in the management of perforating globe injuries was associated with favorable anatomical outcomes, a low rate of postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy, and visual improvement in most patients. This approach represents a viable strategy for addressing the complex challenges in these severe ocular injuries.

records.title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.

content.title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To explore the relationship between the number of retinal lesions observed on ultrawide-field fundus photography (UWF-FP) and the nonperfusion index (NPI) quantified on UWF fluorescein angiography in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

Methods

The NPI was measured on early-phase UWF fluorescein angiography in 100 eyes from 100 patients with PDR, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Eyes were divided into quartiles based on NPI values. Red dots (microaneurysms, retinal hemorrhages, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities), venous beading, cotton-wool spots, and white thread-like arterioles were counted on UWF-FP.

Results

The mean NPI values for quartiles one to four were 2.8 ± 1.1%, 8.5 ± 2.1%, 17.3 ± 4.5%, and 42.8 ± 12.2%, respectively. Eyes in the highest NPI quartile (quartile 4) had significantly fewer retinal lesions on UWF-FP (76.1 ± 50.6) and fewer cotton-wool spots compared with those in the lowest NPI quartile, which showed 253.0 ± 165.5 retinal lesions ( P < 0.001). White thread-like arterioles were present in 80.0% of eyes in quartile four and none in quartile 1. Patients in quartile four were predominantly type 2 diabetics with higher rates of end-stage kidney disease, peripheral neuropathy, lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, and prior limb amputation or revascularization.

Conclusion

In patients with poorly controlled, long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by renal failure, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, or lower-limb amputation, fluorescein angiography should be considered when highly ischemic PDR is suspected, particularly in the presence of white thread-like arterioles, as it may otherwise appear milder on color fundus photography.

records.title: Exploration of Potential Associations Between Sulfated Polysaccharide Exposure and Retinal Findings.

content.title: Exploration of Potential Associations Between Sulfated Polysaccharide Exposure and Retinal Findings.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS), a widely used treatment for interstitial cystitis, has been linked to a distinctive macular toxicity. A recent case report described a similar phenotype with fondaparinux, a related sulfated polysaccharide, raising the possibility of a broader class effect. We explored potential associations between exposure to non-PPS sulfated polysaccharides and retinal imaging findings resembling PPS maculopathy.

Methods

We conducted a single center retrospective study from 2018-2024. Emory Healthcare electronic health records were queried for adults with exposure to fondaparinux, enoxaparin, chondroitin containing products, alginate containing products, and/or dalteparin. Macular imaging during the study period was required for inclusion. A retina specialist reviewed macular imaging for features resembling PPS maculopathy. Given the high number of enoxaparin users with short exposure durations, imaging review for this group was limited to >1 year of documented exposure.

Results

A total of 218 patients were evaluated, including patients exposed to alginate (n = 12), fondaparinux (n = 25), chondroitin sulfate (n = 111), and enoxaparin (n = 70). Mean age at first qualifying macular imaging was 67.4 years and 59.5% were women. There were no cases resembling classic PPS maculopathy. Some patients did exhibit subtle macular pigment alterations without a clear diagnosis [fondaparinux 1 (4.0%); chondroitin sulfate 3 (2.7%); alginate 1 (8.3%)].

Conclusions

This study did not identify a relationship between non-PPS sulfated polysaccharide exposure and the development of macular disease resembling classic PPS maculopathy. Larger studies with increased power may be warranted to determine whether a rare association may be present.

records.title: Post-Pars Plana Vitrectomy Endophthalmitis in Patients with and without Systemic Immunosuppression.

content.title: Post-Pars Plana Vitrectomy Endophthalmitis in Patients with and without Systemic Immunosuppression.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine whether systemic immunosuppression is associated with endophthalmitis after pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), and whether risk varies by drug class and time window.

Methods

Retrospective propensity score matched cohort study using TriNetX, a federated network of 72 US healthcare organizations. Exposed adults undergoing PPV used corticosteroids, classic nonbiologic immunosuppressants, targeted small molecule immunomodulators, or biologics for at least 3 months before surgery; controls had none in the prior year. Matching controlled for demographics, comorbidities, and surgical indication. The outcome was endophthalmitis within 365 days, assessed over early (1-42 days), 1-90 day, and later (43-365 day) windows. Cox modeling was secondary.

Results

After matching, 25,997 patients per cohort were analyzed. No class was associated with endophthalmitis during the early window. During the later window, risk was higher for all immunosuppressants (RR 1.74; 95% CI 1.33 to 2.28; P < .0001), corticosteroids (RR 1.81; 95% CI 1.38 to 2.37; P < .0001), and biologics (RR 2.00; 95% CI 1.00 to 4.03; P = .045). In Cox regression, corticosteroids (HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.01 to 1.39; P = .037) and biologics (HR 1.51; 95% CI 1.08 to 2.11; P = .016) remained independent risk factors.

Conclusion

Systemic corticosteroid use prior to PPV was associated with late-onset endophthalmitis, with excess risk appearing between 43 and 365 days rather than in the early period. This timing is atypical for surgically acquired infection, and some late events may reflect endogenous or inflammatory disease. Immunosuppressed patients may warrant a longer window of suspicion.

records.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.

content.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the treatment outcomes of Type 3 macular neovascularization and identify factors associated with visual outcomes and lesion reactivation during 76 weeks of aflibercept therapy using a treat-and-extend (TAE) regimen.

Methods

This post hoc analysis included 25 treatment-naive patients with Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization who participated in a previous prospective study and received aflibercept treatment for 76 weeks using a TAE regimen. The incidence and outcomes of the first lesion reactivation were assessed. Factors associated with lesion reactivation and best-corrected visual acuity at the final visit were evaluated.

Results

Lesion reactivation occurred in 8 patients (32.0%) during the treatment period; however, no patient experienced a loss of ≥5 letters before or after the first reactivation. In multivariate analysis, best-corrected visual acuity at Week 16 was a strong predictor of final best-corrected visual acuity ( P < 0.001, β = 1.191), and older age was significantly associated with a lower risk of lesion reactivation ( P = 0.036, β = 0.811).

Conclusion

Early visual outcomes after the initial loading injections can serve as reliable prognostic indicators for long-term treatment of Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization using a TAE regimen. In younger patients, the increased likelihood of lesion reactivation should be considered. Although lesion reactivation occurred in approximately one third of the patients, it did not result in significant visual deterioration. Further studies analyzing treatment outcomes in Stage 1 disease are required.

records.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Ultrawide-field (UWF) fundus cameras capture a larger retinal area without pupil dilation. The authors summarized evidence and diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diabetic retinopathy (DR) assessments using UWF images (UWFIs).

Methods

The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science to February 9, 2025, for studies evaluating DR using UWFIs and AI analyses. They followed the PRISMA guidelines and assessed study quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for diagnostic accuracy. Forest plots and summary receiver operating characteristic curves estimated sensitivity and specificity of AI-driven DR screening using UWFI.

Results

Of 527 records identified, 17 studies were included in the systematic review and four in the meta-analysis. All studies used Optos software. Among the included studies, two evaluated DR discrimination from multiple retinal disorders, six addressed DR stage classification based on guideline scales, six evaluated DR screening, and one each focused on referable retinal pathology detection, DR progression prediction, and detection of clinical DR features. The summary sensitivity, specificity, and area under receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-driven DR screening using UWFI were 85.0%, 72.5%, and 0.870 (0.838-0.897), respectively. UWFI-based AI screening showed acceptable sensitivity but limited specificity.

Conclusion

AI-driven DR screening using UWFIs may achieve acceptable sensitivity but with limited specificity; however, these findings should be interpreted with caution, given the limited number of available studies. Further studies using larger, diverse data sets with rigorous external validation across UWF platforms are needed to improve generalizability and clarify the clinical role of UWFI-based AI.

records.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.

content.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term effects of preoperative ectopic inner foveal layer (EIFL) with preserved foveal contour on postoperative retinal microvascular changes in patients with epiretinal membrane.

Methods

Patients were divided into two groups based on EIFL presence: Group 1 without EIFL and Group 2 with EIFL. Superficial and deep vessel densities (SVDs and DVDs), corresponding to the superficial and deep vascular complexes, were quantitatively assessed using OCT angiography.

Results

The SVDs at baseline, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months were 27.9 ± 7.7, 27.6 ± 8.3, 25.9 ± 7.8, 26.1 ± 7.0, and 24.9 ± 8.0% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.075), and 31.6 ± 7.3, 28.0 ± 6.3, 26.7 ± 5.6, 25.4 ± 5.7, and 22.9 ± 5.6% in Group 2, respectively ( P < 0.001). The DVDs were 21.9 ± 4.6, 22.9 ± 4.5, 23.6 ± 5.1, 24.2 ± 4.0, and 23.6 ± 4.7% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.277), and 20.6 ± 4.7, 22.8 ± 4.2, 23.2 ± 3.7, 23.6 ± 5.0, and 23.4 ± 3.8% in Group 2, respectively ( P = 0.003). In the multivariable analysis, baseline BCVA was significantly associated with changes in BCVA in Group 1, whereas in Group 2, baseline BCVA and DVD showed significant associations with BCVA changes.

Conclusion

Patients with EIFL and preserved foveal contour demonstrated more prominent alterations in retinal microvasculature after surgery, and these changes, especially within the deep vascular complex, are considered to play an important role in visual improvement.

records.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.

content.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine whether lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is associated with an increased risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) and retinal tears without detachment (RT) compared with adults without LSC.

Methods

This retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study used TriNetX to compare adults (≥18 years) with LSC to matched adults without LSC. Patients with prior RRD, RT, ocular trauma, or proliferative diabetic retinopathy were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed on demographics, ocular and systemic comorbidities, and prior ophthalmology encounters. Incidence of RRD, RT, the composite endpoint of RRD or RT (RRD/RT), retinopexy, RRD repair, and the composite of RRD repair or retinopexy were compared using risk analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression, yielding risk ratios (RR) and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 64,170 patients per group. LSC patients had significantly higher rates of RRD (RR 8.83, 95% CI 4.86-16.05; p<0.001), RT (RR 10.15, 95% CI 6.79-15.19; p<0.001), and composite RRD/RT (RR 9.60, 95% CI 6.78-13.60; p<0.001). On procedure analysis, retinopexy (RR 6.64, 95% CI 3.52-12.51; p<0.001), RRD repair (RR 4.07, 95% CI 2.27-7.31; p<0.001), and the composite of retinopexy or RRD repair (RR 5.08, 95% CI 3.28-7.87; p<0.001) occurred more frequently in the LSC cohort.

Conclusion

LSC is associated with a substantially increased risk of incident diagnosis of RRD, RT, composite RRD/RT, and their procedural repair after adjustment for known risk factors. These findings suggest LSC may increase the risk of rhegmatogenous retinal pathology.

records.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

content.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings.

Design

Retrospective, multicenter case series.

Patients and methods

This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years).

Main outcome measures

Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype.

Results

Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants.

Conclusions

Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

records.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Subthreshold laser has been proposed as a potentially safer and more effective alternative for patients with acute central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Hence, the objective of this systematic review was to assess the efficacy and safety of subthreshold laser treatment for acute CSC.

Methods

We performed a comprehensive systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from their inception up to March 24, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and/or safety of subthreshold laser against any comparator. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the minimally contextualized GRADE approach.

Results

Six randomized controlled trials (401 participants) in patients with acute CSC were included. Compared with conventional laser, subthreshold laser probably yields similar improvements in visual acuity and reduces retinal pigment epithelium damage but probably leads to a lower rate of subretinal fluid resolution. When compared with observation, subthreshold laser may result in similar visual acuity outcomes but may reduce persistent metamorphopsia and increase subretinal fluid resolution, although the certainty of evidence is very low. Compared with half-dose photodynamic therapy, subthreshold laser may provide comparable visual outcomes but lower anatomical improvement, with very low certainty of evidence.

Conclusion

In acute CSC, subthreshold laser appears safer than conventional laser and produces similar visual outcomes, although its anatomical efficacy is limited. Its potential advantages over observation or photodynamic therapy remain uncertain because of low-certainty evidence.

records.title: 3D corneal and retinal bioprinting: Tissue engineering strategies, translational challenges, and clinical opportunities.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: 3D corneal and retinal bioprinting: Tissue engineering strategies, translational challenges, and clinical opportunities.
content.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with one approach entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

records.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
content.abstract: The molecular basis for vertebrate color vision is expression of spectrally-selective opsin-based photopigments within distinct cone photoreceptor populations. In several primates including humans, and in numerous fish species, genes encoding duplicated, spectrally-divergent cone opsin proteins may be positioned in tandem arrays. This article reviews studies of the regulation of differential expression of these duplicated cone opsin genes in humans and fish, with an emphasis on knowledge derived from the zebrafish model. In humans, the long wavelength-sensitive/medium wavelength-sensitive (LWS/MWS; red/green) tandemly-duplicated array underlies trichromatic color vision; mutations in this array cause altered color vision and retinal degenerations. A foundational model posited that regulation of human LWS vs. MWS opsin expression is stochastic, whereby an upstream enhancer associates randomly with promoters of the proximal or distal gene, and one of these associations becomes permanent. Discoveries of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in teleost fish, including the versatile zebrafish model, led to their use to further pursue mechanisms of differential expression. The tandemly-duplicated zebrafish lws1 and lws2 genes (encoding red-sensing cone opsins) share a common ancestral gene with human LWS and MWS. Subsequent studies revealed that differential expression of these genes is regulated by the paracrine signal retinoic acid (RA) and the endocrine signal thyroid hormone (TH). Further investigations identified additional cone transcripts distinguishing zebrafish LWS1 vs. LWS2 cones, plasticity of cone opsin expression across the lifespan in response to TH, and a candidate receptor and cis-regulatory element. The findings warrant updates to the foundational model and further consideration of hypotheses for regulation of the human LWS vs. MWS genes.

records.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.

content.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize longitudinal patterns of intraretinal (IRF) and subretinal fluid (SRF) dynamics using artificial intelligence-assisted optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarker quantification and to evaluate their association with long-term visual outcomes in eyes with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO).

Methods

Patients with previously treatment-naïve CRVO and a documented 24-month follow-up were retrospectively included. All eyes received intravitreal aflibercept administered according to a treat-and-extend protocol. Spectral-domain OCT scans were analyzed at baseline and after 3 and 24 months. IRF and SRF volumes were quantified using RetinAI Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector (Ikerian AG). Linear regression models were used to assess the association between fluid volumes and 24-month corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA). Patients were clustered according to their IRF trajectories over time to identify distinct fluid-response phenotypes.

Results

Out of 173 patients, 64 eyes (64 patients) were included. Baseline IRF and SRF volumes showed no significant association with 24-month CDVA. Cluster analysis of longitudinal IRF trajectories identified four distinct fluid-response patterns. Eyes with low or rapidly resolving IRF achieved the best long-term visual outcomes (median CDVA 73 letters), whereas those with persistent or recurrent IRF showed poorer outcomes (median 53 letters; P = 0.008). Early IRF resolution tended to predict superior visual recovery at 24 months.

Conclusion

Artificial intelligence-based volumetric OCT analysis suggests that distinct retinal fluid trajectories in CRVO may have prognostic implications for long-term visual acuity, although these findings are preliminary and require validation. Dynamic IRF resolution patterns may be more informative than static fluid volumes for predicting functional outcomes after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy.

records.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

content.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate whether quantitative retinal microvascular and structural parameters, measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), are associated with disease severity and right ventriculo-arterial coupling in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

Results

Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

Conclusion

Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.

records.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.

content.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

Clinical relevance

AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.

Results

Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias.

Conclusion

The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.

records.title: Retina Insurance Reimbursements of Pediatric Retina Patients in a Hospital versus Outpatient Surgical Setting.

content.title: Retina Insurance Reimbursements of Pediatric Retina Patients in a Hospital versus Outpatient Surgical Setting.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate reimbursement patterns for pediatric vitreoretinal procedures performed at a tertiary children's hospital versus an ambulatory surgery center (ASC).

Methods

A retrospective review was conducted of retinal procedures in pediatric patients performed between 1/2022 and 1/2025 at a tertiary children's hospital and an ambulatory surgery center in Texas. Self-pay visits and visits with zero billed charges were excluded. The primary outcome was total median reimbursement percentage based on physician-level services. Secondary outcomes included median reimbursement percentage by payer type, public insurer subgroup, surgical setting, and current procedural terminology (CPT) code. The proportion of visits with zero reimbursement was also evaluated.

Results

394 visits from 282 patients were analyzed, including 219 visits at the children's hospital and 175 at the ASC. Median reimbursement was 34.0% (representing 85% of the equivalent Medicare reimbursement rate). Public insurers reimbursed a higher median percentage than private insurers (35.1% vs. 26.5%, P=0.001). Reimbursement was lower at the hospital than the ASC (29.1% vs 36.3%, P<0.0001). 24.1% of visits received zero payment, occurring more frequently among privately insured than publicly insured visits (30.8% vs. 17.3%, P=0.003). Complex retinal detachment repair reimbursed less for private than public insurers (35.4% vs. 42.7%, P< 0.001).

Conclusion

Private insurers reimbursed lower than public insurers for pediatric vitreoretinal procedures, contrary to patterns commonly reported in adult retinal care. Procedures performed at a tertiary children's hospital resulted in lower reimbursements than those performed at an ASC. Frequent zero-payment encounters, particularly among private insurers, pose challenges that adversely affect the financial sustainability of pediatric retinal care.

records.title: Mechanisms of blood-retinal barrier disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Mechanisms of blood-retinal barrier disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy.
content.abstract: Blood-retinal barrier (BRB) disruption is a common accompaniment of intermediate, posterior and panuveitis causing leakage into the retina and macular oedema resulting in vision loss. It is much less common in anterior uveitis or in patients with intraocular lymphoma who may have marked signs of intraocular inflammation. New drugs used for chemotherapy (cytarabine, immune checkpoint inhibitors, BRAF inhibitors, EGFR inhibitors, bispecific anti-EGFR inhibitors, MET receptor inhibitors and Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors) can also cause different types of uveitis and BRB disruption. As malignant disease itself can cause uveitis, particularly from breast, lung and gastrointestinal tract cancers, it can be clinically difficult to sort out the cause of BRB disruption. Immunosuppression due to malignant disease and/or chemotherapy can lead to infection which can also cause BRB disruption and intraocular infection. In this paper we address the pathophysiology of BRB disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy, methods for estimating the extent and effect of the disruption and examine why some types of intraocular inflammation and malignancy cause BRB disruption and others do not. Understanding this may help sort and manage these patients, as well as devise future therapeutic approaches.

records.title: EFFICIENCY OF LASER PHOTOCOAGULATION ON THE PREVENTION OF RETINAL DETACHMENT IN ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: EFFICIENCY OF LASER PHOTOCOAGULATION ON THE PREVENTION OF RETINAL DETACHMENT IN ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Retinal detachment is a severe complication of acute retinal necrosis, threatening vision. The published articles on the effectiveness of laser in preventing retinal detachment in acute retinal necrosis are controversial. Therefore, we aim to evaluate whether prophylactic laser is effective for retinal detachment after acute retinal necrosis.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched, and the retrieved records were screened. Each included study has well-defined laser-treated group and control group without laser treatment or with enough data for manual grouping. The quality of the included studies was assessed using ROBINS-I ("Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies-of Interventions"). Meta-analysis was conducted to calculate the pooled odds ratios and their 95% confidence interval. Sensitivity analysis was used to test the solidarity, and subgroup analysis was performed to determine the source of heterogeneity.

Results

Fourteen studies with a total of 532 eyes were eventually included. The quality of the included studies was moderate. The combined results showed that the pooled odds ratio was 0.61 (95% confidence interval [0.41∼0.90], P < 0.05, I 2 = 27%). Sensitivity analysis showed that the odds ratios were similar when excluding any study. Subgroup analysis showed moderate heterogeneity among three subgroups (I 2 = 48.0%, P = 0.15 for heterogeneity), and the odds ratio in antiviral therapy and steroid combined with prophylactic laser was 0.43 (95% confidence interval [0.25∼0.74], P < 0.05, I 2 = 0%).

Conclusion

In patients with acute retinal necrosis, laser photocoagulation is an effective treatment to prevent retinal detachment, especially in the subgroup combined with antiviral therapy and steroid.

records.title: INVERTED INTERNAL LIMITING MEMBRANE FLAP TECHNIQUE FOR MACULAR HOLE COEXISTENT WITH RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT.

content.title: INVERTED INTERNAL LIMITING MEMBRANE FLAP TECHNIQUE FOR MACULAR HOLE COEXISTENT WITH RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To report the clinical features and treatment outcomes of patients with macular hole coexistent with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment surgically treated with pars plana vitrectomy and inverted internal limiting membrane flap technique.

Methods

Eleven consecutive patients with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment and macular hole who underwent vitrectomy and internal limiting membrane peeling with the inverted flap technique between December 2017 and February 2021 were retrospectively evaluated. The main outcome measures were retinal reattachment rate, macular hole closure rate, and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity. A nonsystematic literature review was performed to compare the study outcomes with those previously reported.

Results

The primary retinal reattachment rate was 90% (10/11) with one surgery and 100% with 2 surgical procedures. Macular hole closure was achieved in all patients (11/11). All patients showed an improvement in visual acuity at the final postoperative visit, and the mean postoperative best-corrected visual acuity was 0.60 ± 0.32 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (20/80 Snellen equivalent).

Conclusion

Vitrectomy with the inverted internal limiting membrane flap technique achieved not only favorable anatomical retinal reattachment rates but also an encouraging recovery of central macular anatomy and visual function in patients with macular hole coexistent with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

records.title: Genome-Wide Meta-analysis Identifies Risk Loci and Improves Disease Prediction of Age-Related Macular Degeneration.

content.title: Genome-Wide Meta-analysis Identifies Risk Loci and Improves Disease Prediction of Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To identify age-related macular degeneration (AMD) risk loci and to establish a polygenic prediction model.

Design

Genome-wide association study (GWAS) and polygenic risk score (PRS) construction.

Participants

We included 64 885 European patients with AMD and 568 740 control participants (with overlapped samples) in the UK Biobank, Genetic Epidemiology Research on Aging (GERA), International AMD Consortium, FinnGen, and published early AMD GWASs in meta-analyses, as well as 733 European patients with AMD and 20 487 control participants from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA) and non-Europeans from the UK Biobank and GERA for polygenic risk score validation.

Methods

A multitrait meta-analysis of GWASs comprised 64 885 patients with AMD and 568 740 control participants; the multitrait approach accounted for sample overlap. We constructed a PRS for AMD based on both previously reported as well as unreported AMD loci. We applied the PRS to nonoverlapping data from the CLSA.

Main outcome measures

We identified several single nucleotide polymorphisms associated with AMD and established a PRS for AMD risk prediction.

Results

We identified 63 AMD risk loci alongside the well-established AMD loci CFH and ARMS2, including 9 loci that were not reported in previous GWASs, some of which previously were linked to other eye diseases such as glaucoma (e.g., HIC1). We applied our PRS to nonoverlapping data from the CLSA. A new PRS was constructed using the PRS method, PRS-CS, and significantly improved the prediction accuracy of AMD risk compared with PRSs from previously published datasets. We further showed that even people who carry all the well-known AMD risk alleles at CFH and ARMS2 vary considerably in their AMD risk (ranging from close to 0 in individuals with low PRS to > 50% in individuals with high PRS). Although our PRS was derived in individuals of European ancestry, the PRS shows potential for predicting risk in people of East Asian, South Asian, and Latino ancestry.

Conclusions

Our findings improve the knowledge of the genetic architecture of AMD and help achieve better accuracy in AMD prediction.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: Prevalence of Myopic Macular Features in Dutch Individuals of European Ancestry With High Myopia.

content.title: Prevalence of Myopic Macular Features in Dutch Individuals of European Ancestry With High Myopia.
content.abstract:
Importance

High myopia incidence and prevalence is increasing worldwide, and the visual burden caused by myopia is expected to rise accordingly. Studies investigating the occurrence of myopic complications in individuals of European ancestry with high myopia are scarce, hampering insights into the frequency of myopic retinal complications in European individuals and their visual burden.

Objective

To assess the frequency of myopic macular features in individuals of European ancestry with high myopia.

Design, setting, and participants

This cross-sectional analysis of the Dutch Myopia Study (MYST) and individuals with high myopia from the Rotterdam Study (RS) included 626 patients with high myopia (spherical equivalent of refractive error [SER] ≤-6 diopters [D] or axial length [AL] ≥26 mm) who underwent an extensive ophthalmic examination including multimodal retinal imaging. In addition to this combination of a population-based cohort study and mix-based high myopia study, a systematic literature review was also performed to compare findings with studies of individuals of Asian ancestry.

Exposures

High myopia, age, and AL.

Main outcomes and measures

Frequency of myopic macular and optic disc features: tessellated fundus, myopic macular degeneration (MMD), staphyloma, peripapillary intrachoroidal cavitation, peripapillary atrophy (PPA), and "plus" lesions (choroidal neovascularization, Fuchs spot, and lacquer cracks).

Results

The mean (SD) SER of the combined study population (MYST and RS) was -9.9 (3.2) D; the mean (SD) age was 51.4 (15.1) years, and 387 (61.8%) were women. The prevalence of MMD was 25.9% and increased with older age (P for trend <.001), lower SER (odds ratio [OR], 0.70; 95% CI, 0.65-0.76; P < .001), and higher AL (OR, 2.53; 95% CI, 2.13-3.06; P < .001). Choroidal neovascularization or Fuchs spot was present in 2.7% (n = 17), both lesions in 0.3% (n = 2), and lacquer cracks in 1.4% (n = 9). Staphyloma, PPA, and MMD were highly prevalent in visual impaired and blind eyes (frequency was 73.9% [20 of 27], 90.5% [19 of 21], and 63.0% [17 of 27] of unilateral blind eyes for MMD, staphyloma, and PPA, respectively). Seven previous studies in Asian populations reported a variable MMD frequency ranging from 8.3% to 64%, but frequencies were similar for comparable risk profiles based on age and SER.

Conclusions and relevance

In this cross-sectional study of a highly myopic Dutch population of European ancestry, myopic retinal features were frequent; were associated with age, SER, and AL; and occurred in all visually severely impaired eyes. The absence of treatment options for most of these retinal complications emphasizes the need for effective strategies to prevent high myopia.

records.title: MEDIUM-TERM PERFLUORO-N-OCTANE AS RESCUE POSTOPERATIVE TAMPONADE FOR VERY COMPLEX RETINAL DETACHMENTS: ANATOMICAL AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES.

content.title: MEDIUM-TERM PERFLUORO-N-OCTANE AS RESCUE POSTOPERATIVE TAMPONADE FOR VERY COMPLEX RETINAL DETACHMENTS: ANATOMICAL AND FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To report the anatomical and functional outcomes of medium-term perfluoro-n-octane (PFO) tamponade as a rescue procedure in very complex retinal detachments (RDs).

Methods

We reviewed the case records of 35 consecutive patients who underwent vitrectomy for very complex RDs due to diverse etiologies. The surgical complexity was so graded because of the intraoperative failure to ascertain complete retinal reattachment; perfluoro-n-octane was used as rescue tamponade for 2 to 4 weeks. The second intervention included additional membrane peeling, retinectomy, endophotocoagulation, and gas/silicone oil tamponade. The minimum follow-up was 3 months after the final intervention: the primary outcome was retinal reattachment and the secondary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).

Results

The most common presentations were severe trauma with retinal incarceration, preretinal and subretinal hemorrhage, or chronic/recurrent RDs with anterior proliferative vitreoretinopathy. Preoperative BCVA was ≤counting fingers in 31 (88.6%) patients. Complete retinal attachment without any tamponade was achieved in 33 (94.3%) eyes. best-corrected visual acuity improved in 30 (85.7%) eyes: 16 (45.7%) had BCVA ≥20/200 and 21 (60%) regained ambulatory vision (≥5/200). Two eyes developed keratopathy, and four needed antiglaucoma medications.

Conclusion

We achieved excellent anatomical outcomes and acceptable functional outcomes in nearly inoperable RDs with few side effects. Medium-term perfluoro-n-octane tamponade can be used as a salvage procedure in very complex RDs where intraoperative reattachment cannot be ensured.

records.title: Effect of Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy on the risk for retinal detachment after cataract surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy on the risk for retinal detachment after cataract surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy on the incidence of pseudophakic retinal detachment (RD). The PubMed and Embase databases were searched for meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to study location, number of cases, mean follow-up time, and cataract procedure. The final analysis included 11 studies with 309 cases of RD in 65 117 eyes undergoing cataract surgery. Among them, 8232 eyes underwent Nd:YAG capsulotomy. This analysis demonstrated an increased risk for RD with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy (relative risk [RR], 1.57; 95% CI, 1.17-2.12; P = .003; hazard ratio, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.03-2.62; P = .04). Subgroup analysis suggested somewhat stronger associations in Asian (RR, 4.54; 95% CI, 2.20-9.38; P < .0001) than in non-Asian populations (Americans, P = .12; Europeans and others, P = .21) and with extracapsular cataract extraction (RR, 2.97; 95% CI, 1.83-4.83; P < .0001) than with phacoemulsification (P = .95). To conclude, Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy may be associated with an increased risk for pseudophakic RD.

records.title: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS FOR OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY IN AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

content.title: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS FOR OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY IN AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To survey the current literature regarding applications of deep learning to optical coherence tomography in age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

Methods

A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses systematic review was conducted from January 1, 2000, to May 9, 2021, using PubMed and EMBASE databases. Original research investigations that applied deep learning to optical coherence tomography in patients with AMD or features of AMD (choroidal neovascularization, geographic atrophy, and drusen) were included. Summary statements, data set characteristics, and performance metrics were extracted from included articles for analysis.

Results

We identified 95 articles for this review. The majority of articles fell into one of six categories: 1) classification of AMD or AMD biomarkers (n = 40); 2) segmentation of AMD biomarkers (n = 20); 3) segmentation of retinal layers or the choroid in patients with AMD (n = 7); 4) assessing treatment response and disease progression (n = 13); 5) predicting visual function (n = 6); and 6) determining the need for referral to a retina specialist (n = 3).

Conclusion

Deep learning models generally achieved high performance, at times comparable with that of specialists. However, external validation and experimental parameters enabling reproducibility were often limited. Prospective studies that demonstrate generalizability and clinical utility of these models are needed.

records.title: Identification of novel biomarkers for retinopathy of prematurity in preterm infants by use of innovative technologies and artificial intelligence.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Identification of novel biomarkers for retinopathy of prematurity in preterm infants by use of innovative technologies and artificial intelligence.
content.abstract: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of preventable vision loss in preterm infants. While appropriate screening is crucial for early identification and treatment of ROP, current screening guidelines remain limited by inter-examiner variability in screening modalities, absence of local protocol for ROP screening in some settings, a paucity of resources and an increased survival of younger and smaller infants. This review summarizes the advancements and challenges of current innovative technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and predictive biomarkers for the diagnosis and management of ROP. We provide a contemporary overview of AI-based models for detection of ROP, its severity, progression, and response to treatment. To address the transition from experimental settings to real-world clinical practice, challenges to the clinical implementation of AI for ROP are reviewed and potential solutions are proposed. The use of optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA) technology is also explored, providing evaluation of subclinical ROP characteristics that are often imperceptible on fundus examination. Furthermore, we explore several potential biomarkers to reduce the need for invasive procedures, to enhance diagnostic accuracy and treatment efficacy. Finally, we emphasize the need of a symbiotic integration of biologic and imaging biomarkers and AI in ROP screening, where the robustness of biomarkers in early disease detection is complemented by the predictive precision of AI algorithms.

records.title: Myopia: Histology, clinical features, and potential implications for the etiology of axial elongation.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Myopia: Histology, clinical features, and potential implications for the etiology of axial elongation.
content.abstract: Myopic axial elongation is associated with various non-pathological changes. These include a decrease in photoreceptor cell and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cell density and retinal layer thickness, mainly in the retro-equatorial to equatorial regions; choroidal and scleral thinning pronounced at the posterior pole and least marked at the ora serrata; and a shift in Bruch's membrane opening (BMO) occurring in moderately myopic eyes and typically in the temporal/inferior direction. The BMO shift leads to an overhang of Bruch's membrane (BM) into the nasal intrapapillary compartment and BM absence in the temporal region (i.e., parapapillary gamma zone), optic disc ovalization due to shortening of the ophthalmoscopically visible horizontal disc diameter, fovea-optic disc distance elongation, reduction in angle kappa, and straightening/stretching of the papillomacular retinal blood vessels and retinal nerve fibers. Highly myopic eyes additionally show an enlargement of all layers of the optic nerve canal, elongation and thinning of the lamina cribrosa, peripapillary scleral flange (i.e., parapapillary delta zone) and peripapillary choroidal border tissue, and development of circular parapapillary beta, gamma, and delta zone. Pathological features of high myopia include development of macular linear RPE defects (lacquer cracks), which widen to round RPE defects (patchy atrophies) with central BM defects, macular neovascularization, myopic macular retinoschisis, and glaucomatous/glaucoma-like and non-glaucomatous optic neuropathy. BM thickness is unrelated to axial length. Including the change in eye shape from a sphere in emmetropia to a prolate (rotational) ellipsoid in myopia, the features may be explained by a primary BM enlargement in the retro-equatorial/equatorial region leading to axial elongation.

records.title: Structure and function of ABCA4 and its role in the visual cycle and Stargardt macular degeneration.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Structure and function of ABCA4 and its role in the visual cycle and Stargardt macular degeneration.
content.abstract: ABCA4 is a member of the superfamily of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters that is preferentially localized along the rim region of rod and cone photoreceptor outer segment disc membranes. It uses the energy from ATP binding and hydrolysis to transport N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (N-Ret-PE), the Schiff base adduct of retinal and phosphatidylethanolamine, from the lumen to the cytoplasmic leaflet of disc membranes. This ensures that all-trans-retinal and excess 11-cis-retinal are efficiently cleared from photoreceptor cells thereby preventing the accumulation of toxic retinoid compounds. Loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding ABCA4 cause autosomal recessive Stargardt macular degeneration, also known as Stargardt disease (STGD1), and related autosomal recessive retinopathies characterized by impaired central vision and an accumulation of lipofuscin and bis-retinoid compounds. High resolution structures of ABCA4 in its substrate and nucleotide free state and containing bound N-Ret-PE or ATP have been determined by cryo-electron microscopy providing insight into the molecular architecture of ABCA4 and mechanisms underlying substrate recognition and conformational changes induced by ATP binding. The expression and functional characterization of a large number of disease-causing missense ABCA4 variants have been determined. These studies have shed light into the molecular mechanisms underlying Stargardt disease and a classification that reliably predicts the effect of a specific missense mutation on the severity of the disease. They also provide a framework for developing rational therapeutic treatments for ABCA4-associated diseases.

records.title: Studies of the retinal microcirculation using human donor eyes and high-resolution clinical imaging: Insights gained to guide future research in diabetic retinopathy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Studies of the retinal microcirculation using human donor eyes and high-resolution clinical imaging: Insights gained to guide future research in diabetic retinopathy.
content.abstract: The microcirculation plays a key role in delivering oxygen to and removing metabolic wastes from energy-intensive retinal neurons. Microvascular changes are a hallmark feature of diabetic retinopathy (DR), a major cause of irreversible vision loss globally. Early investigators have performed landmark studies characterising the pathologic manifestations of DR. Previous works have collectively informed us of the clinical stages of DR and the retinal manifestations associated with devastating vision loss. Since these reports, major advancements in histologic techniques coupled with three-dimensional image processing has facilitated a deeper understanding of the structural characteristics in the healthy and diseased retinal circulation. Furthermore, breakthroughs in high-resolution retinal imaging have facilitated clinical translation of histologic knowledge to detect and monitor progression of microcirculatory disturbances with greater precision. Isolated perfusion techniques have been applied to human donor eyes to further our understanding of the cytoarchitectural characteristics of the normal human retinal circulation as well as provide novel insights into the pathophysiology of DR. Histology has been used to validate emerging in vivo retinal imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography angiography. This report provides an overview of our research on the human retinal microcirculation in the context of the current ophthalmic literature. We commence by proposing a standardised histologic lexicon for characterising the human retinal microcirculation and subsequently discuss the pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying key manifestations of DR, with a focus on microaneurysms and retinal ischaemia. The advantages and limitations of current retinal imaging modalities as determined using histologic validation are also presented. We conclude with an overview of the implications of our research and provide a perspective on future directions in DR research.

records.title: Unraveling ptosis: A comprehensive review of clinical manifestations, genetics, and treatment.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Unraveling ptosis: A comprehensive review of clinical manifestations, genetics, and treatment.
content.abstract: Ptosis is defined as an abnormally low-lying upper eyelid margin on the primary gaze, generally resulting from a congenital or acquired abnormality of the nerves or muscles that control the eyelid. Ptosis can occur alone or concurrently as an ocular or systemic syndrome, and the prevalence of ptosis varies among different countries and populations. Isolated ptosis typically causes aesthetic problems in patients and can lead to functional ophthalmic problems in severe cases. In individuals with syndromic ptosis, ptosis can be a warning of serious medical problems. There are different approaches to classification, depending on the onset time or the etiology of ptosis, and the clinical characteristics of congenital and acquired ptosis also differ. Pedigree and genetic analysis have demonstrated that hereditary ptosis is clinically heterogeneous, with incomplete concordance and variable expressivity. A number of genetic loci and genes responsible for hereditary isolated and syndromic ptosis have been reported. Optimal surgical timing and proper method are truly critical for avoiding the risk of potentially severe outcomes from ptosis and minimizing surgical complications, which are challenging as the pathogenesis is still indistinct and the anatomy is complex. This review provides a comprehensive review of ptosis, by summarizing the clinical manifestations, classification, diagnosis, genetics, treatment, and prognosis, as well as the bound anatomy of upper eyelid.

records.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dynamic in vivo capsular apposition to the intraocular lens (IOL) in highly myopic eyes after capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT), and to investigate its correlation with in-the-bag IOL behavior.

Setting

Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

Design

Prospective randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Highly myopic patients undergoing cataract surgery were randomized to receive CTR implantation or not. SS-OCT was performed at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to assess capsular apposition. Postoperative aqueous depth (PAD), IOL rotation, and anterior and posterior capsular opacification (ACO/PCO) were evaluated at each follow-up visit.

Results

A total of 29 eyes with CTR implantation and 30 eyes without CTR were included. The CTR group exhibited accelerated anterior capsular apposition, demonstrated by a smaller lens-anterior capsule distance (LCD) at 1 day and a higher proportion of anterior capsular apposition at 1 week. From 1 month onward, posterior capsular apposition occurred more frequently in the CTR group. At 1 day, the average LCD positively correlated with both PAD and IOL rotation. During subsequent follow-up period, the mean capsular bend index exhibited negative correlations with the absolute changes in PAD and IOL rotational speed. The CTR group developed less severe ACO, eyes with incomplete posterior capsular apposition had a higher risk of PCO.

Conclusions

CTR implantation facilitates accelerated anterior and more complete posterior capsular apposition to the IOL in highly myopic eyes, which may contribute to improved postoperative IOL stability and a reduced incidence of capsular opacification.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To improve the accuracy of refractive prediction for pediatric secondary sulcus intraocular lens (IOL) implantation by optimizing the effective lens position (ELP) prediction within the SRK/T formula.

Setting

Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Guangzhou, China.

Design

Retrospective consecutive case-series.

Methods

The value of sulcus-ELP was identified by linear regression formula with utilizing back-calculated ELP. The obtained sulcus-ELP was subsequently incorporated into the original SRK/T formula, then creating the sulcus-SRK/T formula. The prediction accuracy of sulcus-SRK/T formula was compared with six formulas. Main outcome measures included prediction error (PE), mean error (ME), median absolute error (MedAE), and the percentage of eyes with prediction error within ±0.50 diopters (D) and ±1.00 D.

Results

This study included 86 pediatric patients (131 eyes) who underwent secondary ciliary sulcus IOL implantation. With the modified formula, the percentages of eyes achieving the prediction error (PE) within ±0.50 D and ±1.00 D were 25.6% and 53.9%, respectively, significantly higher than those of other formulas. The mean error (ME) of the modified formula was 0.46±1.39 D, and the modified formula showed lower median absolute error (MedAE) (0.95 D, P < .05) than other formulas.

Conclusions

By optimizing ELP prediction of the SRK/T formula, the prediction accuracy of pediatric secondary sulcus IOL implantation has been improved. The sulcus-SRK/T formula is a worthwhile choice and requires further external validation to confirm its effectiveness.

records.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare iridocorneal angle (ICA) and other anterior segment anatomical parameters between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same anterior chamber depth (ACD), which could have important implications for hyperopic posterior chamber phakic intraocular lens (PC-pIOL) implantation.

Setting

Private eye hospital.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

ACD, ICA, anterior chamber volume (ACV), white-to-white (WTW), and spherical equivalent were obtained from records of patients aged 21-55 and analysed using paired and regression approaches. Hyperopic and myopic eyes were matched 1:1 by ACD and compared with paired t-tests. Analysis of covariance was performed with ICA as the dependent variable, refractive group as the fixed factor and ACD as a covariate. An ICA ≥ 35 degrees was defined as a sufficiently wide angle.

Results

Forty-four hyperopic and 72 myopic eyes were included. In the paired analysis, ICA and ACV did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.356 and 0.446 respectively). In the regression analysis, refractive group was not a significant predictor of ICA after adjustment for ACD (p = 0.193). The proportion of eyes with wide ICA increased with ACD but did not differ between groups.

Conclusion

We found no statistically significant anatomical difference in Scheimpflug-measured ICA and ACV between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same ACD in this population. Nevertheless, the current thicker hyperopic lens design without a central hole remains an important reason for exercising greater caution with hyperopic PC-pIOL implantation.

records.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the demographic, ocular, systemic, and histopathologic features of patients undergoing surgery for late intraocular lens (IOL) instability with clinically suspected dead bag syndrome (DBS).

Setting

Private ophthalmology practice and tertiary ophthalmic pathology laboratory.

Design

Single-center consecutive case series with prospective tissue collection and retrospective chart review.

Methods

Capsular bag remnants were explanted during secondary IOL surgery and submitted for histopathologic examination. Demographic, ocular, and systemic characteristics were obtained from the medical record. Lens epithelial cell (LEC) status was graded as 0 = absent; 1 = rare residual LECs; 2 = focal identifiable LEC segments. Specimens were assessed for capsular splitting/schisis, cortical material, and anterior capsular fibrous metaplasia. Exploratory clinical comparisons were performed between LEC grade 0 and LEC grade 1-2 subgroups.

Results

Thirty-one eyes from 26 patients underwent secondary IOL surgery for late IOL subluxation or dislocation with clinical suspicion of DBS, including 27 with histopathologic evaluation. Mean age at secondary surgery was 70.5 ± 10.5 years and 80.7% patients were male. Median time from cataract surgery to presentation was 13.0 years (IQR 9.0-16.5). Axial myopia was present in 6/31 eyes (19.4%). Atopy was documented in 9/31 (29.0%), prior radiation or chemotherapy exposure in 8/31 (25.8%), autoimmune disease in 10/31 (32.3%), and ACE inhibitor or ARB use in 14/31 (45.2%). Complete LEC absence (grade 0) was present in 8/27 (29.6%), while 19/27 (70.4%) demonstrated residual LECs and/or cortical material (grades 1-2). Spontaneous posterior capsular rupture was documented in 15/31 (48.4%) cases and in 15/27 (55.6%) histopathology-confirmed cases. Atopy was more frequent in LEC grade 0 than among LEC grade 1-2 eyes (37.5% vs 15.8%; P = 0.32), though this did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

DBS represents a histopathologically definable spectrum of capsular degeneration characterized by LEC depletion and capsular splitting with structural failure leading to late IOL instability. Nearly half of confirmed cases presented without clinically evident spontaneous posterior capsular rupture, suggesting that rupture is not required for DBS diagnosis.

records.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.

Setting

10 European study centers.

Design

Prospective observational multicenter study.

Methods

Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.

Results

In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.
